title: Kestrel Closed-End Consumer Lease: Computing the Excess Mileage Charge
content:
**Lease-end billing clause — the excess mileage charge, Kestrel Closed-End Consumer Lease**

**Clause.** The excess mileage charge is the miles driven — the turn-in odometer reading less the odometer reading at delivery — less the mileage allowance — the annual mileage allowance times the sum of the lease term in months and the maturity extension months used, divided by 12 and rounded down to a whole mile — never below zero, charged at the lease's excess mileage rate per mile and rounded to the nearest cent with a half cent rounded up (0.0001 cent is added before rounding so that an amount lying exactly on a half cent rounds up). The miles below zero are not carried: when the miles driven do not exceed the allowance, the miles charged are zero and there is no charge.

**Quantities and their records**

| Quantity | Taken from |
|---|---|
| Odometer at delivery, turn-in odometer | the lease record |
| Annual mileage allowance, lease term in months, maturity extension months used | the lease record |
| Excess mileage rate per mile | the rate recorded on the lease at booking |

**Worked examples (all inputs hypothetical)**

1. Annual allowance 12000 miles, term 36 months, no extension months: allowance 36000 miles. Odometer at delivery 12; turn-in odometer 41249; miles driven 41237. Miles charged 5237. At $0.25 per mile the charge is $1309.25.
2. Annual allowance 10000 miles, term 36 months, 1 extension month used: 10000 times 37 divided by 12 is 30833.33…, rounded down to 30833 miles. Miles driven 31000; miles charged 167. At $0.20 per mile the charge is $33.40.
3. Annual allowance 15000 miles, term 24 months: allowance 30000 miles. Miles driven 28400; miles charged zero; no charge.
